title: VA HB171: Student instruction; Internet safety, policy to include key modern digital safety topics.

obligations: Review, amend if necessary, and approve the school division's acceptable use policy for the Internet every two years (Sec. A).

Include in the policy provisions designed to prohibit use by division employees and students of the division's computer equipment and communications services for sending, receiving, viewing, or downloading illegal material via the Internet (Sec. A(i)).
Include in the policy provisions that seek to prevent access by students to material that the school division deems to be harmful to juveniles as defined in § 18.2-390 (Sec. A(ii)).

Select a technology for the division's computers having Internet access to filter or block Internet access to child pornography as set out in § 18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in § 18.2-372 (Sec. A(iii)).
Establish appropriate measures to be taken against persons who violate the policy (Sec. A(iv)).

Include a component on Internet safety for students integrated in the division's instructional program that includes instruction on key modern digital safety topics, including online scams, misinformation, and content generated by artificial intelligence (Sec. A(v)).
Post the school division's policy on its website in accordance with § 22.1-253.13:7 (Sec. A).
Certify compliance with these requirements annually to the Department of Education (Sec. A).
The superintendent shall take such steps as he deems appropriate to implement and enforce the division's policy (Sec. B).

The principal or other chief administrator of any private school that satisfies the compulsory school attendance law pursuant to § 22.1-254 and accepts federal funds for Internet access shall select a technology for its computers having Internet access to filter or block Internet access to child pornography as set out in § 18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in § 18.2-372 (Sec. C).

The Superintendent of Public Instruction shall issue guidelines to school divisions regarding instructional programs related to Internet safety that includes guidance on the topics specified in clause (v) of subsection A (Sec. D).

What it does

Requires each local school board in Virginia to review and approve an acceptable internet use policy every two years, with minimum provisions including filtering or blocking child pornography and obscenity, prohibiting illegal material, establishing measures against violators, and providing internet safety instruction on online scams, misinformation, and artificial intelligence generated content. It also requires certain private schools to filter or block child pornography and obscenity, and directs the Superintendent of Public Instruction to issue guidelines on the required internet safety topics.

Who it applies to

  • Local school boards and public school divisions
  • Division employees and students
  • Superintendents
  • Principals or chief administrators of private schools that satisfy the compulsory school attendance law pursuant to § 22.1-254 and accept federal funds for Internet access
  • Superintendent of Public Instruction

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • not stated in the text

Obligations

  • Review, amend if necessary, and approve the school division's acceptable use policy for the Internet every two years (Sec. A).
  • Include in the policy provisions designed to prohibit use by division employees and students of the division's computer equipment and communications services for sending, receiving, viewing, or downloading illegal material via the Internet (Sec. A(i)).
  • Include in the policy provisions that seek to prevent access by students to material that the school division deems to be harmful to juveniles as defined in § 18.2-390 (Sec. A(ii)).
  • Select a technology for the division's computers having Internet access to filter or block Internet access to child pornography as set out in § 18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in § 18.2-372 (Sec. A(iii)).
  • Establish appropriate measures to be taken against persons who violate the policy (Sec. A(iv)).
  • Include a component on Internet safety for students integrated in the division's instructional program that includes instruction on key modern digital safety topics, including online scams, misinformation, and content generated by artificial intelligence (Sec. A(v)).
  • Post the school division's policy on its website in accordance with § 22.1-253.13:7 (Sec. A).
  • Certify compliance with these requirements annually to the Department of Education (Sec. A).
  • The superintendent shall take such steps as he deems appropriate to implement and enforce the division's policy (Sec. B).
  • The principal or other chief administrator of any private school that satisfies the compulsory school attendance law pursuant to § 22.1-254 and accepts federal funds for Internet access shall select a technology for its computers having Internet access to filter or block Internet access to child pornography as set out in § 18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in § 18.2-372 (Sec. C).
  • The Superintendent of Public Instruction shall issue guidelines to school divisions regarding instructional programs related to Internet safety that includes guidance on the topics specified in clause (v) of subsection A (Sec. D).

Prohibitions

  • Use by division employees and students of the division's computer equipment and communications services for sending, receiving, viewing, or downloading illegal material via the Internet (Sec. A(i)).
  • Access by students to material that the school division deems to be harmful to juveniles as defined in § 18.2-390 (Sec. A(ii)).
  • Access through division computers having Internet access to child pornography as set out in § 18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in § 18.2-372 (Sec. A(iii)).
  • Access through private school computers having Internet access to child pornography as set out in § 18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in § 18.2-372 for private schools that satisfy the compulsory school attendance law and accept federal funds for Internet access (Sec. C).

Penalties and enforcement

The policy must establish appropriate measures to be taken against persons who violate the policy (Sec. A(iv)). The superintendent shall take such steps as he deems appropriate to implement and enforce the division's policy (Sec. B). No specific penalties, fines, or private right of action are stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • A public school division deploying or using AI must ensure its acceptable use policy includes instruction on content generated by artificial intelligence as part of the required internet safety component (Sec. A(v)).
  • The Superintendent of Public Instruction will issue guidelines to school divisions on instructional programs related to internet safety, including guidance on AI-generated content topics, which may shape how AI-related instruction is implemented (Sec. D).
  • The law does not impose direct requirements on AI developers or on organisations deploying AI outside the school instructional context (Sec. A, Sec. D).

Notable exemptions

  • Private schools that do not satisfy the compulsory school attendance law pursuant to § 22.1-254 or do not accept federal funds for Internet access are not subject to the filtering or blocking requirement in Sec. C (Sec. C).
  • No other exemptions are stated in the text.

Compliance steps

  • Review, amend if necessary, and approve the school division's acceptable use policy for the Internet every two years (Sec. A).
  • Ensure the policy contains the required provisions: prohibition on illegal material, prevention of access to harmful-to-juveniles material, filtering or blocking child pornography and obscenity, measures against violators, and internet safety instruction on online scams, misinformation, and AI-generated content (Sec. A(i)-(v)).
  • Post the policy on the division's website in accordance with § 22.1-253.13:7 (Sec. A).
  • Certify compliance annually to the Department of Education (Sec. A).
  • The superintendent implements and enforces the policy (Sec. B).
  • For a private school that satisfies the compulsory school attendance law and accepts federal funds for Internet access, select technology to filter or block child pornography and obscenity (Sec. C).
  • Monitor and incorporate guidelines issued by the Superintendent of Public Instruction on internet safety topics including AI-generated content (Sec. D).

2026 SESSION ENROLLED VIRGINIA ACTS OF ASSEMBLY -- CHAPTER An Act to amend and reenact § 22.1-70.2 of the Code of Virginia, relating to student instruction; internet safety; certain topics. [H 171] Approved Be it enacted by the General Assembly of Virginia: 1. That §  22.1-70.2 of the Code of Virginia is amended and reenacted as follows: §  22.1-70.2 . Acceptable internet use policies for public and private schools. A. Every two years, each local school board shall review, amend if necessary, and approve the school division's acceptable use policy for the Internet internet . At a minimum, the policy shall contain provisions that (i) are designed to prohibit use by division employees and students of the division's computer equipment and communications services for sending, receiving, viewing, or downloading illegal material via the Internet internet ; (ii) seek to prevent access by students to material that the school division deems to be harmful to juveniles as defined in §  18.2-390 ; (iii) select a technology for the division's computers having Internet internet access to filter or block Internet internet access through such computers to child pornography as set out in §  18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in §  18.2-372 ; (iv) establish appropriate measures to be taken against persons who violate the policy; and (v) include a component on Internet internet safety for students that is integrated in a division's instructional program that includes instruction on key modern digital safety topics, including online scams, misinformation, and content generated by artificial intelligence . The policy may include such other terms, conditions, and requirements as deemed appropriate, such as requiring written parental authorization for Internet internet use by juveniles or differentiating acceptable uses among elementary, middle, and high school students. Each school division's policy shall be posted on its website in accordance with §  22.1-253.13:7 . Additionally, each local school division shall certify compliance with these requirements annually to the Department of Education. B. The superintendent shall take such steps as he deems appropriate to implement and enforce the division's policy. C. In addition to the foregoing requirements regarding public school Internet internet use policies, the principal or other chief administrator of any private school that satisfies the compulsory school attendance law pursuant to §  22.1-254 and accepts federal funds for Internet internet access shall select a technology for its computers having Internet internet access to filter or block Internet internet access through such computers to child pornography as set out in §  18.2-374.1:1 and obscenity as defined in §  18.2-372 . D. The Superintendent of Public Instruction shall issue guidelines to school divisions regarding instructional programs related to Internet internet safety that includes guidance on the topics specified in clause (v) of subsection A .
